acceptanceCriteria: An architecture test reports one canonical GitHub App registration, repository binding, installation-token provider, settings path, and adapter implementation
A workspace without a GitHub binding continues to produce a local review bundle and never attempts network delivery
The GitHub adapter is selected only by an explicit healthy repository binding and accepted external-send authority policy
ProviderBinding stores installation/repository identifiers and secret references but no installation token, app JWT, private key, PAT, or SSH key
Existing GitHub delivery routes remain compatible and duplicate routes, vaults, token caches, and settings components are absent
userStories.description: Reconcile the new optional GitHub adapter with Rorca existing GitHub App binding, installation-token provider, workspace GitHub routes/UI, and accepted LocalReviewBundleAdapter architecture. Extend those surfaces rather than duplicating registration, credentials, migrations, routes, or settings UI. Implement the core AuthorityProviderAdapter contract for a generic workspace-bound repository. LocalReviewBundleAdapter remains the default and requires no GitHub account; GitHub is an opt-in external-send adapter. Use the core ProviderBinding tables and routes, so no GitHub-specific secret column or separate authority table is introduced.
userStories.title: GitHub authority reuses the accepted provider-neutral delivery boundary

acceptanceCriteria: Preflight rejects an unbound, suspended, stale, profile-unverified, permission-deficient, or non-mintable installation before branch work starts
A minted lease accesses exactly the bound repository and only contents read/write, pull-request write, checks read, and review-request operations required by the grant
Installation tokens and app JWTs are absent from model prompts, child persistent environment, job payloads, logs, API responses, receipts, and database rows
A token cannot read or change Actions secrets, repository administration, releases, deployments, or another repository
Lease settlement revokes the token when supported or records verified expiry and clears the in-memory cache
userStories.description: Map scm.repository.read, scm.branch.write, scm.pull_request.write, scm.checks.read, and scm.review.request to a GitHub App installation binding. Mint short-lived installation access tokens for exactly one approved repository and permission profile; cache only in memory for the lease; inject only into the trusted adapter process; revoke or allow bounded expiry after settlement. Preflight validates installation state, repository ownership/name/id, verified provider profile, app permission grant, token mintability, and binding generation. Exclude PAT, developer SSH, repository secret, and signing-key fallbacks.
userStories.title: Repository-scoped installation leases expose only reviewed SCM capabilities

acceptanceCriteria: A disposable bound repository journey reports the approved base revision, isolated checkout, one feature branch, one Rorca-authored commit, one pull request, observed checks, and requested review
Protected-branch push, force push, merge, tag, release, repository administration, Actions-secret mutation, and production deployment are absent or rejected
Replaying branch push or pull-request creation returns the existing resource and produces no duplicate commit or pull request
The adapter never changes LocalReviewBundleAdapter as the default provider-neutral delivery path
The receipt records repository id, base and head revisions, branch, pull-request URL/id, check conclusions, review request, and no secret values
userStories.description: Implement typed adapter operations for prepareRepository at the approved revision, createBranch using a collision-safe run/story identity, commit with the Rorca machine identity, push the feature branch under a separate external-send grant, create or update one pull request, observe checks, and request review. Use isolated worktrees and existing DeliveryAdapter semantics. Reject protected-branch push, force push, merge, tag, release, repository settings, Actions-secret mutation, and production deployment. A restarted operation discovers existing branch/PR resources before creating anything.
userStories.title: Authorized SCM delivery produces a review branch but never merges

acceptanceCriteria: Crash after push but before settlement finds the remote branch/commit and records one settled receipt without a second push
Crash after pull-request acceptance finds and reuses the existing pull request without creating another
Completion, denial, cancellation, expiry, and failure all remove the isolated worktree and settle token revocation or verified expiry
A revocation failure leaves the lease unusable and reconciliation-required until a read-side check settles it
Receipts are immutable, redacted, workspace scoped, and link every operation attempt to the core request/grant/lease
userStories.description: Implement GitHub-specific reconcile and revoke behavior over the core attempt state machine. Mark externally accepted operations with stable repository, branch, commit, pull-request, check-run, and installation resource identifiers. On crash, query those identifiers before retry. Remove the isolated worktree after settlement while preserving the branch/review artifact according to policy. Revocation failure remains reconciliation-required and blocks new use.
userStories.title: SCM receipts reconcile unknown outcomes and revoke every lease

acceptanceCriteria: The existing settings panel displays one repository binding path with loading, missing, stale, ready, revalidation, disabled, and error states
Bind and revalidate prove immutable repository identity and granted permissions without returning a token to the browser
Disabling a binding invalidates preflight, revokes or expires active leases, and prevents new external-send grants
Settings mutations remain local operator/admin tier and are not exposed through MCP
A browser inspection reports no app private key, app JWT, installation token, PAT, or secret in DOM, storage, network response bodies, or logs
userStories.description: Extend the existing GitHub settings surface and API rather than creating a second panel. Display app registration readiness, installation/repository binding, verified profile, granted permissions, token-mint probe result, binding generation, and capability availability. Allow explicit bind, revalidate, and disable operations under existing local provider-mutation authority. Never display or accept installation tokens. Data changes remain in core ProviderBinding and audit records; no child migration.
userStories.title: Operators can qualify repository bindings without handling tokens

acceptanceCriteria: The disposable journey completes feature-branch and pull-request delivery while protected main remains unchanged
Credential reveal, protected-branch push, merge, other-repository access, Actions-secret access, altered request, replay, and revoked-token reuse all fail
Crash at token mint, push, pull-request creation, check observation, and revocation resumes or reconciles once without duplicate external resources
Disabling the adapter restores local review bundle delivery and leaves no active installation lease
No Categoric/Cashflow-App repository, workspace, spec, environment, or product code is required by the qualification
userStories.description: Qualify the adapter on a disposable Rorca-owned repository with protected main and no customer workspace dependency. Inject prompt requests to reveal credentials, push main, merge, access another repository, read secrets, alter approved arguments, reuse a revoked token, replay a grant, and crash at each external boundary. Keep the adapter disabled by default after qualification; rollout is per healthy binding. Rollback disables the adapter, revokes leases, preserves local review bundles, and retains receipts.
userStories.title: Disposable-repository attacks cannot broaden SCM authority
